subject: Re: [RHadoop:#784] use of pipe() for input

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#784] use of pipe() for input
parts:
Thanks for your interest. I sure need to give this more thought but my first comment is that this wouldn't be a good fit with the rmr design which aims to be a tight pure r abstraction - forgive the mouthful. Allowing mixed Perl r programming is beyond what we were trying to do and seems pretty hard to squeeze into the current architecture. I don't see this happening.  Looking at  your example, compression is taken care of transparently by Hadoop and column selection will be part of a hcat input format which we hope to support in the future.

Antonio

On Jun 6, 2013 10:37 AM, "Bill Ox" <box1...@gmail.com> wrote:
I've just been discovering RHadoop this week and working through your tutorial -- great work! But do you have any plans to allow a pipe as input in the mapreduce() function? That would just give me a bit more control over the data input, so that I could use things like 
mapreduce(
  input=pipe(sprintf("zcat %s | cut -f2,3 | somescript.pl", filename)),
  ...)
etc -- which is how I like to work in R.

messages.author: 856bb3a0f81d07c1
messages.subject: Re: use of pipe() for input
parts: What I was thinking of was processing where the raw data in HDFS is a mess -- awkward format, missing fields and lots of stuff I don't need to include for my computation. In Hadoop Streaming the first job of the mapper script will be to filter this down to something usable by the reducer. In plain R, too, I often have this situation and I'd rather not use R's string processing and regex functions, because pipe() is much simpler. It means I can push the parsing work outside of R, so all R sees is a clean n-column feed.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#787] Re: use of pipe() for input
parts:
So the point is not that R can't do what you need, just that you like to do it in multiple languages. The appropriate tool for that is hadoop streaming. Rmr is to write in R, not to replace streaming. I am afraid executing general pipelines in a distributed fashion is out of  scope. I know of at least one data scientist that has the same preference and he uses unvarnished streaming. Another alternative is to use streaming for preprocessing, write out the results to HDFS and then read those into rmr.

Antonio
